description: Positive employment and self-employment income fall by the shift share; the same weighted total is added to positive capital income (gains, interest, dividends and rent) in proportion to the capital income each person already receives. Static, current law, no behavioral response. State net revenue is state income tax plus use tax, less refundable state credits and the state benefits in gov.household.household_state_benefits (for California: SSP, CAPI, child care subsidies, CVRP, CARE, FERA and three Los Angeles programs; no Medi-Cal or CalWORKs); California's employee SDI contribution is reported separately. Federal net revenue is the all-government change less every state's net change and less state payroll taxes (employee and employer) and local taxes, which the all-government total counts but no state's line holds; federal_net_published_definition_change_b keeps them, as the published site does. Each shifted branch prices Medicaid enrollees at the baseline's cost per enrollee (the baseline's medicaid_slcsp_state_denominator), so state Medicaid totals move with enrollment. The *_with_health_tanf fields also charge each state its share of Medicaid, CHIP and Medicare Savings Program costs under federal matching rules (state_benefit_cost), the whole cost of coverage it funds alone for people whose immigration status rules out federal matching (CHIP coverage through the unborn-child option keeps its federal match), its own health subsidies (for California, the Covered California premium subsidy; Healthier Oregon only for people not also enrolled in Medicaid) and the TANF change its line doesn't already hold (CalWORKs for California; Massachusetts's TAFDC already sits in its state benefits), since the federal TANF block grant is fixed; the all-government total adds every program in healthcare_benefit_value and counts TANF once. The shift sets employment_income and self_employment_income on each branch, so anything that reads their *_before_lsr inputs sees pre-shift earnings: the default TANF earned-income list and Massachusetts's, Montana's and South Carolina's lists, so those states' TANF benefits don't respond and the TANF, other-states and all-government lines miss that response (SNAP's gross self-employment income reads them too). California's CalWORKs list reads the shifted variables. 'levels' allocate the new capital income across the country, as the published sweep does; 'within_state_levels' give each state's freed labor income to that state's own capital holders.
